KONF.1.1.rationale: Process/policy for configuration management. The flake repo with review and CI is the technical foundation, but the policy itself is organizational.

KONF.1.2.rationale: Periodic review of the policies; organizational.

KONF.1.3.rationale: Documentation of config tools and their origin; flake.lock pins provenance, the documentation is organizational.

KONF.1.4.rationale: Access restriction on configuration documentation (git repo permissions); outside the NixOS config.

KONF.1.5.rationale: Secrets in config should be encrypted (sops-nix/agenix). Cannot be detected generically; KONF.2.3 already rejects plaintext user passwords.

KONF.2.1.rationale: The NixOS configuration is the documented baseline; documenting it is up to the user.

KONF.2.2.rationale: SSH only. The guidance defers to established algorithms; we use BSI TR-02102-4 (2026-01) tables 2-5 as that standard. sshd and the ssh client are limited to the listed key exchange, cipher, MAC and signature algorithms (OpenSSH names), host keys are ECDSA only, rekey after 1 GB/1 h. Consequences: Ed25519, Curve25519 and RSA are not in the TR and are rejected. diffie-hellman-group15-sha512 has no OpenSSH equivalent. Encrypt-then-MAC HMAC variants and sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 are accepted as the same primitives (our interpretation). Not covered: TLS and other protocols, disk encryption algorithms, DH group size in /etc/ssh/moduli.

KONF.2.3.rationale: Plaintext passwords in the config are rejected. Well-known default hashes cannot be detected.

KONF.2.4.rationale: Disables Bluetooth, FireWire, rarely used network protocols/filesystems (kernel modules), avahi, printing and the default package set. List is a starting point, not exhaustive. Deviations via keepKernelModules and keepServices. Not covered: weak crypto algorithms (KONF.2.2), unneeded users, firmware features.

KONF.2.5.rationale: The flake in git is the reference state and the system closure is immutable. Asserted: system.configurationRevision is set (nixos-version --configuration-revision) and not a dirty tree unless allowDirty. Not covered: mutable state outside the closure (/var, unmanaged /etc files, imperative changes) is not compared against the reference.

KONF.2.7.rationale: Level erhöht, optional (KANN). Sovereign tooling is a procurement decision.

KONF.2.8.rationale: Level erhöht, optional. Alternative admin access (e.g. serial/out-of-band) is deployment specific.

KONF.2.9.rationale: Level erhöht. Assert Secure Boot is active (e.g. lanzaboote) when the option is available; exempt for VMs.

KONF.3.1.rationale: A TPM 2.0 is the cryptographic hardware storage. The TPM2 stack (security.tpm2: udev rules, tss group owning /dev/tpmrm0) is enabled and asserted, so systemd-cryptenroll, systemd-creds and services can use it; the VM test uses an emulated TPM. Hardware or VMs without TPM set the requirement exempt. Not covered: whether a TPM is present and whether keys are actually stored in it (cannot be seen at evaluation time).

KONF.3.2.rationale: At least one boot.initrd.luks.devices entry must exist (fileSystems.<n>.encrypted and disko LUKS layouts create one). Encryption invisible to the NixOS configuration (ZFS native, bcachefs, self-encrypting drives) is declared in otherEncryption. Unencrypted cloud volumes need an exemption. Not covered: that every persistent filesystem is on an encrypted device, and the LUKS cipher (TR-02102-1). Booting from LUKS is not VM-tested.

KONF.3.5.rationale: Location determination, optional (KANN); not meaningful for servers.

KONF.3.7.rationale: Restrict attached peripherals: services.usbguard and/or blacklist usb-storage. Needs an allowlist option per deployment.

KONF.3.8.rationale: Disables automounters: udisks2, devmon, gvfs, autofs. Manual mounts stay possible and are not forced to noexec. Desktops will need an opt-out.

KONF.4.1.rationale: Directory service attachment depends on the organization (SSSD/LDAP); not generically enforceable.

KONF.4.2.rationale: Resolvers must be authorized. Plan: option listing allowed resolvers, assert networking.nameservers/resolved DNS is a subset.

KONF.4.3.rationale: SSH only. Public key authentication only; password, keyboard-interactive, empty-password and host-based authentication are off. Other remote maintenance protocols (RDP, SNMP, vendor tools) are not covered.

KONF.4.4.rationale: SSH only. No root login, login restricted to allowGroups (default wheel), TCP/agent/X11 forwarding, gateway ports and tunnels off unless allowForwarding is set. Deploy tools need a normal admin user with sudo instead of root. Lockout guard: evaluation fails if no user in allowGroups has an authorized key (ECDSA when KONF.2.2 is on).

KONF.4.5.rationale: Authorized time sources are listed in allowedTimeServers (no default). networking.timeServers and timesyncd NTP=/FallbackNTP= are set to it; timesyncd, chrony and ntpd are asserted to use only listed servers. Not covered: NTP servers from DHCP (networkd UseNTP, dhcpcd), ntpd-rs custom sources, authenticated NTP (NTS).

KONF.5.1.rationale: Every login must authenticate: users.allowNoPasswordLogin false, no console autologin, no user with an empty hashed password, no PAM service accepting empty passwords. The login PAM service is forced to false because NixOS enables it by default. Covered by the eval assertion test and the profile check only: NixOS VM tests cannot enable it, since the test driver uses an empty root password. Screen lock and MFA are not covered (BER.5.9).

KONF.5.2.rationale: Guidance is about users being logged in with several identities at once; no config-level rule on a server. Revisit if desktop scope is added.

KONF.6.1.rationale: Minimal privileges for applications: systemd sandboxing defaults for services we manage, plus AppArmor. Large; split per service later.

KONF.6.2.rationale: File server role only; handle in a role-specific module (Samba/NFS).

KONF.6.4.rationale: sudo executable only for group wheel, sudo asks wheel members for a password (opt-out allowPasswordlessSudo), su requires wheel. privilegeEscalation = run0 replaces sudo with systemd run0 (polkit, no setuid sudo). Not covered: role-based administration (KANN), inventory of setuid wrappers.

KONF.6.5.rationale: Level erhöht, optional (KANN). Dynamic access control means context-dependent access decisions (device state, location, time, data classification) under a fixed policy. That is an identity/application-level mechanism; AppArmor or SELinux are static mandatory access control and do not implement it, so there is no generic NixOS setting for it.

KONF.6.16.rationale: Virtualization hosts only; handle with a virtualization role.

KONF.7.1.rationale: Malware scanning on file access: ClamAV (services.clamav, on-access). Needs an agreed scope of paths.

KONF.7.3.rationale: Level erhöht. Host-based detection (auditd rules, AIDE); verify which options nixpkgs provides.

KONF.7.4.rationale: Level erhöht. Network IDS is usually a separate system.

KONF.7.5.rationale: Alerting on malware findings. Assert a notification path (mail/webhook) is configured once 7.1/7.2 exist.

KONF.7.7.rationale: Level erhöht. Periodic test of the scanner (EICAR); operational procedure.

KONF.7.8.rationale: Level erhöht. Multiple scan engines; product decision.

KONF.7.9.rationale: Software is installed through the Nix daemon: nix.settings.allowed-users is limited to allowedUsers (default root and @wheel), and neither allowed-users nor trusted-users may contain "*". The system closure is read-only. Not covered: users downloading and running binaries in writable locations such as /home (see KONF.7.10).

KONF.7.10.rationale: noexec,nosuid,nodev on /tmp (tmpfs), /var/tmp (bind mount) and /dev/shm. Opt-out via keepExec; Nix builds in /tmp need it. Not covered: application allowlisting (AppArmor/SELinux, code signing), data mounts such as /home or /srv (site specific).

KONF.7.11.rationale: Level erhöht. Library execution control; no standard NixOS mechanism.

KONF.7.12.rationale: Level erhöht. Script execution control; no standard NixOS mechanism.

KONF.7.13.rationale: Level erhöht. Per-service systemd SystemCallFilter; part of per-service hardening (see 6.1).

KONF.7.14.rationale: Module signature enforcement. NixOS kernels do not sign modules by default; investigate security.lockKernelModules and a signed-kernel option first.

KONF.7.15.rationale: Host firewall is enabled and asserted. Outbound allowlisting is application-specific and not enforced.

KONF.7.16.rationale: Interpretation: kernel exploit mitigations. Sysctl limits (kptr_restrict, dmesg_restrict, unprivileged BPF, BPF JIT hardening, ASLR, ptrace_scope, perf_event_paranoid), hardened boot parameters (slab_nomerge, init_on_alloc/free, page_alloc.shuffle, randomize_kstack_offset, vsyscall=none), page table isolation, kexec disabled. Contradicting user settings are reported via assertions.

KONF.8.1.rationale: system.autoUpgrade must be enabled; centrally pushed deployments (CI, colmena, deploy-rs) set the requirement exempt. autoUpgrade only finds updates that reach the flake lock file; bumping inputs is up to the user. Notifying administrators is not covered.

KONF.8.2.rationale: Applications are part of the NixOS closure, so system.autoUpgrade must be enabled and activate updates (operation switch, or boot with allowReboot). Not covered: software updated outside Nix (containers, language package managers), and updates only arrive once the lock file is bumped.

KONF.9.1.rationale: Guidance: limit storage for non-system services via quotas/separate filesystems. Plan: assert separate /var and /home mounts or quotas.

KONF.9.2.rationale: Level erhöht. Host CPU limits for guests; part of virtualization role.

KONF.9.3.rationale: Level erhöht. Redundant components for critical functions; architecture decision.
